newsitem.title: UK: UK assay office increase hallmarking in 1996.
newsitem.headline: UK assay office increase hallmarking in 1996.

text.p: The number of gold items hallmarked at the four UK assay offices last year rose 3.4 percent over 1995 to 18,238,185.
Of the total 10.83 million(up 5.4 percent) were manufactured domestically and 7.40 mllion (up 22 percent) were of foreign origin.
The biggest percentage rises came in 14 carat gold items which showed a 61-percent gain in total to 241,678 hallmarked pieces.
Of that total, foreign items rose 61 percent against 1995 imports to 60,060 and the number of domestically fabricated items rose 52.7 percent to 181,617.
By weight, the total gold hallmark rose 1.1 percent to 76,939,449 grams.

The 31,015 platinum items hallmarked showed a rise of 659.1 percent over 1995. The number of foreign-fabricated items rose 2,759.5 percent to 1,675 and there was an 80-percent rise in UK-fabricated platinum items to 29,339 items.
Silver items hallmarked rose eight percent to 5,326,041 of which 1.66 million (up 22 percent) were foreign fabrications and 3.67 million (up 2.7 percent) were domestically fabricated.

By weight, the platinum items hallmarked at 208,706 grams was a rise of 597.7 percent on 1995 while the 124,792 grams of silver items passing through the assay offices represented a 16.2 percent increase over 1995.
